question.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy+8y$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-2).$

current_example.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y) = x^2 + 2y^2 +x$ that passes through the point where $(x,y) = (1, 1).$
current_example.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y) = (1,1)$ can be found by computing $\nabla f(1,1).$  

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y) = (1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+x)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}+x)\,j \\  & =(2x+0+1)\,i+(0+4y+0)\,j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i+4y\,j \\ ∇f(1,1) & =(2(1)+1)\,i+4(1)\,j \\  & =3\,i+4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we want a unit normal vector, we normalize $\nabla f(1,1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(1,1)}{‖∇f(1,1)‖} & =\frac{3\,i+4\,j}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\,i+4\,j)\end{aligned}
$$
